thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache eviction/paging spike detected across r-gpu-pool-7. Paging > 85% sustained for 7m, continuous-batching throughput abnormal.

maya (oncall): seeing it too. dashboards show cache size growth + sustained read latencies. any obvious recent rollouts?

alex (eng-runtime): rolled model-quant-q4 to r-gpu-pool-7 ~30m ago but perf was green in canary. attaching logs.

sam (eng-sre): logs look like repeated full-cache misses + heavy prefetch storm. continuous batching seems to be amplifying "shared prefix" requests and causing multiple large KV loads.

jess (eng-ml): streaming routes are experiencing token cadence stalls too - some streams are hanging at 0.5-1s/token where normal is ~40ms. suspect partial flush interactions with KV eviction.

maya (oncall): customers reporting slow responses and a couple 504s from hosted API. li, can you surface the largest affected accounts?

li (customer-success): pinged top 3 customers in NA and EU. preliminary: two enterprise customers seeing latency spikes on chat generation, one reported interruptions in streaming. I told them we're triaging and will follow up.

sam (eng-sre): immediate mitigation plan idea: 1) reduce continuous-batching window + max_batch_tokens to cut amplification, 2) throttle prefetcher, 3) temporarily disable continuous batching on streaming endpoints to avoid token cadence stalls. anyone object?

alex (eng-runtime): agree. I can patch runtime config and push a hotfix. config snippet I'm proposing:

```
# runtime-hotpatch
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  batch_window_ms: 6   # decreased from 20
  max_batch_tokens: 1024  # decreased from 8192
kv_cache:
  prefetch_threads: 4  # decreased from 16
streaming:
  continuous_batching: false  # disable for streaming routes
  partial_flush: false
```

sam (eng-sre): +1. also add a guard to drop prefetch for entries > 512KB to avoid huge page pulls.

maya (oncall): do it. alex, please also add a quick health-check that rejects any request that would cause a synchronous full-cache read > 200ms. we want to fail-fast rather than stall.

alex (eng-runtime): applying hotpatch now. running `kubectl -n r-runtime patch cm runtime-config --patch "$(cat hotpatch.yaml)"` then rolling deploy on r-gpu-pool-7.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by alex. Rolling update r-runtime/serving -> 6 pods updating.

maya (oncall): monitoring metrics. paging rate dropping already. prefetch CPU down ~45%.

sam (eng-sre): logs show reduction in concurrent KV pulls. continuous batch size distribution moved left (median tokens per batch ~600 now).

li (customer-success): update from customers: one reported immediate improvement in chat latency, streaming interruptions reduced. they're still seeing occasional partial stalls on long sessions.

jess (eng-ml): partial stalls trace shows a race where partial_flush flushes out the prefix while a streaming request expects KV to be present -> stall and then synchronous load. temporary disable seems to reduce incidence. will instrument a fix.

maya (oncall): current impact: 3% elevated latency (p95) across hosted API in NA for the last 20m, 0.7% increased error rate (504/503). region-wise: NA and EU primarily.

sam (eng-sre): can we run a quick throttling script to limit continuous-batch concurrency per pod? I can push a qps limiter to runtime.

alex (eng-runtime): pushed qps limiter to 10 per pod for batch creation. deploy-bot: new config applied.

deploy-bot: Config patch applied. No pod restarts required.

maya (oncall): metrics look stable for 12m. paging down to baseline. streaming token cadence stable where continuous_batching disabled.

li (customer-success): I'll send a short status update to affected customers: root cause + mitigation + ETA for full fix.

jess (eng-ml): next steps: 1) revert the aggressive prefetch and replace with size-aware prefetch, 2) fix partial_flush race (PR incoming), 3) end-to-end test for streaming+kv eviction. assigning owners.

sam (eng-sre): creating an incident ticket and postmortem stub. tagging runtime/kv/cache and streaming teams.

maya (oncall): handing off to morning oncall (alex will coordinate the remainder). summary for handoff: paging spike due to amplification from continuous batching + large prefetches after model rollout. mitigations applied: reduce batch window & tokens, throttle prefetch, disable continuous batching for streaming routes, qps limiter. customer impact: elevated p95 ~3%, small error increase; improvements visible.

alex (eng-runtime): noted. I'll follow up with PRs and perf regression test.

li (customer-success): I'll keep customers updated with ETA for full fix (ETA 48h).

incident-bot: Incident ticket created INC-2026-4827, severity: S2, owner: eng-runtime.

maya (oncall): thanks team. continue monitoring; if paging resurges escalate to S1.

sam (eng-sre): action items captured: [sam] add size guard to prefetcher, [jess] PR partial_flush fix, [alex] perf test and postmortem draft, [li] customer comms.

maya (oncall): handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
